top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) are a mature, repeatedly reproduced achievement: magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms took frequency measurement to the 10^-18 level and opened precision tests of gravity, constants and many-body physics. The two-laureate allocation matches the invention and realisation, and the citation scope is clear and well supported by the whole committee. An award is clearly preferable to no award.
recusal_note: No direct conflict apparent from profile; as an atomic-physics theorist I have a field affinity and collaborate with atomic and attosecond groups, but none with Katori or Ye is documented.
